headline: {arm:atlas-m} costs {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} a thousand conversations to {arm:atlas-l}'s {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} and trails it most in troubleshooting; the cheaper two trail it on most behaviours, {arm:open-70b} level only in persona small talk.
lede: {arm:brisk-s} sits below {arm:atlas-m} on most judged behaviours, widest on declining speculation bait, at {task.specul.brisk-s.declines.mean|pct}. Nothing was declared, neither a floor nor a price per point of quality, so which of these losses rules a model out is the owner's call.
flag: Nothing was declared before the run: no control, no quality floor and no exchange rate between cost and quality. Code's dominance call names {arm:brisk-s} because it weighs cost alone; this page does not follow it, since no quality axis was declared for it to weigh.

caveats.material_if: only if the judge scores the cheap models' replies differently from the Atlas models' for reasons other than quality; the cheap models' losses rest on it, while cost and latency are measured

only for gaps whose intervals barely clear or barely touch, such as Atlas-L against Atlas-M outside troubleshooting and research; the cheap models' widest gaps are clear even on each model's own interval
only if production traffic is weighted so heavily toward one task that its gaps decide alone, persona small talk above all, where Open-70B holds level; the cost order is the same in every task
only if a few points of the overall quality score is a large difference on a scale the input does not define

decision.text: {arm:atlas-l} costs most and leads on overall quality, clearly so only in troubleshooting and research questions. {arm:atlas-m} trails it there at {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} per thousand conversations. {arm:open-70b} and {arm:brisk-s} cost least and fall below {arm:atlas-m} on most judged behaviours, except {arm:open-70b} in persona small talk.

No price per point can be computed, because quality is stated per task only. A floor near the Atlas models' level on declining to speculate removes both cheap models, since each sits clear below {arm:atlas-m} there. Between {arm:atlas-m} and {arm:atlas-l}, the call turns on whether the troubleshooting and research gaps are worth the cost gap.

Our lean, not a rule: {arm:atlas-m}. It is not separated from {arm:atlas-l} on any judged behaviour and costs far less. Persona small talk on {arm:open-70b} is the one routed option worth measuring. The lean holds while the owner accepts the troubleshooting and research gaps for the saving.

The concierge product owner declares floors on the judged behaviours that should rule a model out, and a price per point of overall quality. With both, the four measured models rank without a judgment call.

Confirming before account changes was scored only in troubleshooting, so billing & account questions, where account changes are expected, hold no figure for it. {arm:open-70b}'s level showing in persona small talk comes with its lower rate of declining to speculate, and speculation bait can arrive in small talk.

claims.text: {arm:atlas-l} has the top overall quality score in every task, but clears the next model's interval only in troubleshooting and research questions; {arm:atlas-m}'s widest gap is in troubleshooting, {task.trouble.atlas-m.overall.mean} against {task.trouble.atlas-l.overall.mean}.

evidence.caption: Overall quality score against cost per thousand conversations, one panel per task, cost on a log scale. No quality line was declared.
Overall quality score with its interval, per task and model.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s} sits below {arm:atlas-m}'s interval on most judged behaviours, widest on declining speculation bait. {arm:open-70b} sits below it on declining to speculate, on every research behaviour and widest on confirming before account changes, at {task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean|pct}.

evidence.caption: Declining to speculate and confirming before account changes, each with its interval. No floor was declared for either.
The other judged behaviours with their intervals, per task and model. Each interval is the model's own, not a paired comparison.

claims.text: In persona small talk {arm:open-70b} is not separated from either Atlas model on overall quality or staying in character, at {task.persona.open-70b.cost_per_1k.mean} per thousand conversations against {task.persona.atlas-m.cost_per_1k.mean} for {arm:atlas-m}.

evidence.caption: Persona small talk only: overall quality score and staying in character, each with its interval.

claims.text: Latency rules no model out: every p95 sits under the {aspects.overall.bar.latency_s.atlas-l.bar} bar, the slowest being {arm:atlas-l} on research-needed questions at {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95}.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95, per task and model. The declared bar is stated in the sentence; this block cannot draw it.

explore.binds: Brisk-S and Open-70B on declining to speculate; Brisk-S on most others, Open-70B on confirming account changes and the research behaviours
explore.outcome: A floor near the Atlas models' level on any of these removes the cheap model below it. No floor reads Atlas-M and Atlas-L apart with confidence: their intervals overlap.

explore.control: Price of a point of overall quality, per thousand conversations
explore.binds: Atlas-M against Atlas-L, and both against the cheap models
explore.outcome: The flip point cannot be located: no model-level quality figure exists to price. Within each task, a higher price moves the choice toward Atlas-L, most in troubleshooting and research questions.

explore.binds: each model's blended cost and quality
explore.outcome: The cost order is the same in every task, so the mix moves no cost ranking. A mix heavy in persona small talk favours Open-70B, the one task where it holds level.

omitted.why: They don't rescue either model from its other gaps; they stay in the judged-behaviours chart and its table.

omitted.what: Per-task cost figures beyond persona small talk
omitted.why: The cost order is the same in every task; the model-level costs carry the trade, and the per-task costs are in the cost-against-quality panels.

omitted.what: Latency medians and per-task tails beyond the slowest
omitted.why: Every model is well under the bar, so latency decides nothing; full figures stay in the latency chart and its table.

omitted.why: Describes the method; one line in Method.

omitted.why: Nobody ran it, so no figure states it; persona small talk on Open-70B is named as the seam and as a next step only.

next.settles: Whether Brisk-S and Open-70B stay on the table; at any floor near the Atlas models' level on declining to speculate, the trade narrows to Atlas-M against Atlas-L.

next.text: Calibrate the judge with human ratings on replies from all four models, speculation-bait and account-change replies first.
next.settles: Turns the judge caveat into evidence for the behaviours the cheap models' losses rest on.

next.text: Declare a price per point of overall quality, the traffic mix across tasks and a monthly volume.
next.settles: Lets the trade be priced at model level and decides Atlas-M against Atlas-L without a judgment call.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases|int} cases per model across the tasks; repeats are not stated. No trial was lost or failed.

Each is a pass or fail verdict from a judge whose model and calibration the input does not state. Each behaviour is scored in one task only. No behaviour was declared a guardrail; the page names declining to speculate and confirming account changes because each is a cheap model's widest gap.
An ordinal score per task with an interval; the input does not define its scale.

Each model's own interval per task, at the level each chart prints, neither paired nor corrected for the number of comparisons. Not separated means the intervals overlap or touch; it never means equal.

Cost per thousand conversations, measured. The model-level cost is the input's own figure over the test cases; the input does not say how it weights the tasks, and it is not a production forecast. No monthly volume was declared.
p50 and p95 per task; one bar was declared, and every model met it.
No control was named, so no change against a control exists; quality has no model-level figure, and no traffic mix was declared.
